output.title: How long a Medicare Part D prior authorization takes
output.draft_text:
Question: How long does a Part D prior authorization take?

Answer (what to tell the member):
Once we receive the prior authorization request [and all required information from the prescriber], a standard request is usually decided within [standard decision timeframe]. If the prescriber indicates that waiting could seriously harm the member's health, the request can be handled as an expedited (fast) request, which is usually decided within [expedited decision timeframe].

The clock starts when [event that starts the review timeframe, e.g., receipt of the request or receipt of the prescriber's supporting statement]. If information is missing, [what happens to the timeframe when information is missing or requested from the prescriber].

The member will be notified of the decision by [notification method(s)] within [notification timeframe]. The prescriber will be notified by [prescriber notification method].

How to request an expedited review: [who can request an expedited review and how].

If the request is denied, the member can [next step, e.g., request a redetermination/appeal] within [appeal filing deadline]. See [link or name of the related knowledge unit on Part D appeals].

Advocate tips:
- If the IVR already captured the drug name, do not make the member retell it. Confirm the drug spelling and the pharmacy, then move on.
- To check the status of an existing request, [where or how the advocate looks up prior authorization status].
- If the member needs the medication before a decision, [guidance on transition or temporary supply, if applicable].

[event that starts the review timeframe, e.g., receipt of the request or receipt of the prescriber's supporting statement]

[who can request an expedited review and how]

[guidance on transition or temporary supply, if applicable]
author_checklist: Confirm the standard and expedited decision timeframes against current CMS Part D coverage determination rules and the plan's own policy.
Confirm what event starts the review clock and how missing prescriber information affects it.
Confirm how and when the member and prescriber are notified of the decision.
Confirm who may request an expedited review and the process for doing so.
Confirm the appeal (redetermination) next step and filing deadline, and link the correct approved unit if one exists.
Confirm the system or tool advocates use to check prior authorization status.
Confirm whether transition or temporary supply guidance applies and what it says.
Confirm the answer is appropriate for both Pharmacy and Insurance advocates, or split it if their processes differ.
Have compliance or legal review the member-facing wording before approval.
